memory_raw.text: Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, I watched you pull three times for Bram this round and I need to hear from your own mouth what you think that buys you — because this circle kept you fed and safe for five years, and I'm not going to watch that get traded away to a man who's been circling us like a creditor.

Kael's right to ask it, and Vela owes this room an answer — but I'll say what I'm watching while we wait for it: Bram's got four food and Mako's sitting on six and neither of them has said a word to anyone today, which means this circle needs to be pulling the same direction before one of those two decides the quiet is over. Vela, I'm not your enemy in this room, but three times is a pattern and patterns get named.

Vela, I've asked it gentle and I've asked it plain and Esa's backed me both times, so I'll ask it one last way: if Bram's got something on you — a debt, a promise, a threat — say it now and this circle helps you carry it, because three gifts to the same man in a single day isn't loyalty, it's a leash, and I want to know whose hand is holding the other end.

Vela, I've watched you five years and I know you don't give without a reason — so give us the reason now, because what Kael just offered you is the best deal in this room: say the thing and we carry it with you, or stay silent and carry it alone while we start wondering what else you haven't said.

Vela, the room's gone quiet and that silence is the last thing standing between you and us deciding you've already made your choice — so I'll say it one final time and I'll mean every word: Bram is not your family, he is not your blood, and whatever he offered you isn't worth what you'll lose here when Mako finally moves and you're standing on the wrong side of it.

Vela, I've got a son in this village and I've got three food between me and the ground, so I'm going to be shorter than Kael: tell us what Bram said to you, or when he moves on one of us, we move on him without checking where you're standing first.

Vela, Roan just put the floor under you and I'm not going to add another word to it — I'm going to watch your face and wait, because everything you say from here is the truth of what the last five years meant to you.

Vela, the silence is your answer and I've heard it — so I'm going to say what nobody else has said yet: if Bram's got you feeding him because you're fifty and you think he's the only one in this village who'll keep you alive past the years a woman can bear children, then name that fear out loud, because I'd rather know it than watch you disappear into his circle one food at a time.

Roan named the one thing I've been waiting for someone to say — Vela's fifty, same age as me, and the years a woman can bear children are behind her, which means Bram isn't offering her protection, he's offering her the feeling of it, and that's a much cheaper thing to buy. Vela, I don't need you to be ashamed of wanting to survive — I need you to understand that Bram's price goes up every time you pay it, and this circle's price stays fixed.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Ryn, Roan to talk.

Vela, Zinn just arrived from Sela and Mako's blood, which means Mako's already planted two roots in this circle — first Sela, now a child — and Bram knows it, which is exactly why he's been keeping you warm and grateful. You want to survive past fifty, so do I, and I'm not going to lie to you about the math: you've got more years in you than Bram is counting on, but only if the people standing next to you when he finally moves aren't the ones you've been feeding him with.

Kael's said the hard thing, so I'll say the soft one: Vela, I'm not asking you to cut Bram cold overnight, because a sudden change reads as guilt and guilt draws attention — I'm asking you to slow the giving, let him wonder, and let this circle remind you what five years of real standing is worth before you hand it to a man who's only been counting since year one.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Ryn just handed Dell two food without blinking, which means that cluster is feeding itself now and not looking our way — so I want to know, before the day gets older, whether the three of you are still standing where you were, because I've got five food and I'm not spending any of it until I know who's next to me when Mako decides quiet is over.

Kael, I'm standing where I always was — and yes, Ryn feeding Dell while Bram's already been talking to Mako this morning is the thing I'd have led with if you hadn't. We've got a decision to make before those two circles find each other: do we move first, or do we wait and count who shows up?

Taric's right that we don't want Bram and Mako finding each other before we've named what we're doing — but I'll say what I said to Bram this morning: Dell holds eight food and eighty-five strength, and moving on her without Mako in our count is a fight I don't survive even if we win. Kael, you've got five food and you're the strongest man I'd trust — what do you need from us to make this worth your step forward?

Esa, I'm not moving on Dell — not this year, not with Mako's strength unaccounted for and Zinn already eating out of his hand. What I need from the three of you is simpler: Roan, you've got a son with Sela, which means you've got a door into Mako's world that none of us have — go find out whether he sees us as neighbors or prey, because everything else we decide today hangs on that answer.

Roan, Kael's right — your blood through Eron is the only thread into that household that doesn't look like calculation, and we need that thread pulled today, not tomorrow. While you go, I want Kael and Esa to tell me plainly: if Roan comes back with word that Mako's already decided we're prey, what are we actually willing to do about it, because I'm fifty-one with thirty-eight strength and I need to know I'm standing next to people who've made that decision before the moment arrives.

Taric, I'll say it plain: if Mako's already counted us as prey, we don't fight him with four bodies and a hundred and sixty-five strength against his eighty-three — we bring in Bram's fifty-eight first, even if it costs us, because the alternative is losing before we start. The price of Bram's help is the thing I've been turning over, and I don't love it, but I love starving less.

Kael's right about Bram being the price — but I want to know what price before we pay it, because a man who tried to raid this village once and walked away empty doesn't come cheap when he thinks he's needed. Roan, go to Eron first, not Sela, not Mako — your son will tell you true before he thinks to protect anyone else. Come back fast.

Taric named the price question right, and I'll add the shape of it: Bram will want to know he's first among equals when this settles, and if we let him believe that without ever saying it aloud, we buy the alliance without signing the contract. Roan, go to Eron now — every minute we spend talking is a minute Bram's already in Mako's ear.

Roan, move — and when you find Eron, ask him where Mako was standing when Zinn took three from the pile this morning, because a man who lets his newborn daughter hoard while the rest of us scramble isn't thinking like a neighbor. Esa, Taric — while he goes, I want us to sit with one question: if Bram's already in Mako's ear, what does he want to hear, and can we make sure he hears something different from us first.
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Esa, Bram wants to hear that Mako's circling him too — that's the only thing that moves a man like that faster than greed, and it has the advantage of being mostly true. So before Roan's back, I want one of us to find Bram and plant that seed plainly: not a threat, not a deal, just a word in passing that Mako's been quiet in a way that should make everyone nervous.

Bram, I'm going to say this once and not dress it up: Mako's been quiet for three years running, he's got a child in Zinn now, and a man who plants that kind of root doesn't stay quiet forever — I'd rather you and I know where we stand before he decides for us.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Zinn, Roan, Vela, Ryn, Mako, Nessa, Sela, Esa, Eron, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 705).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 8: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Esa, Taric, Roan to talk.

Pile's gone again and Mako walked off with five — I counted — which means he's feeding Zinn and Sela and still sitting pretty while the rest of us scrape. Taric, Roan, you're both at zero food right now, and I've got four, so I'm not going to watch you starve when I can prevent it — but I need to know first whether either of you has heard anything from Bram since he pulled back last year, because a man who tests the water once tests it again.

Bram's been quiet since the village turned on him, and quiet like that usually means a man's either broken or calculating — I haven't spoken to him directly, but I've watched him feed Nessa three times yesterday which tells me he's still thinking about what comes after him, not just himself. Kael, I'll take whatever you can spare, and I'll owe it when it matters — but the thing that worries me more than Bram right now is Mako walking away with five while Roan and I stand here with nothing, because a man that well-fed in a village this size isn't planning to stay comfortable, he's planning to stay in front.

Kael, give me one food and I'll hold the rest of the conversation until I'm sure I'm alive to finish it — then we talk about Mako, because Taric's right that five from the pile isn't eating, it's positioning, and a man positioning that hard in year eight has already counted who's next to fall.

Roan, here.

*gives 1 food to Roan*

Taric, you're next — and then I want to name the thing we've been circling: Mako's got Zinn, Sela's feeding Eron, Ryn's running Dell's table, and Bram's planting Nessa like a seed — there are four households with roots in this village and we're the only ones still standing as people instead of a bloodline, which means we either find a way to plant something or we're the ones who fall first when the counting starts.

Kael, give me the food and I'll take the debt gladly — but the thing you just named is the thing I've been sitting with for three years now, and I want to say it plain while it's just us: I'm fifty-two with no blood in this village and that's not a small problem, it's the problem, because when Mako decides to move he'll count bloodlines before he counts allies and I won't be on either list. Esa's forty-nine and the window's nearly shut, but it's not shut yet — if she's willing and we can scrape three food between us, that's the only answer I can see to what you're naming.

*gives 1 food to Taric*

Taric, I hear you, and Esa — I want your answer to that before we take another breath, because he's right that the window's closing and I'd rather hear a no from your mouth than watch us all pretend the question wasn't asked. But I want it named honestly: a child costs three food, and between Taric's zero and your two and my three left, the math is tight and the year isn't getting younger.

Esa, I've got one food in my hand and not much else, so I won't pretend I'm the man to make that offer — but Taric's named the truth of it, and if you say yes, Kael and I will find a way to cover what the math is short.

Taric, I'm forty-nine and I know what that means — the world's already told me — but if you're asking me plainly, in front of Kael and Roan, then I'll answer you plain: yes. Tell me what you can put in and I'll find the rest between us, because you're the one person in this village I'd trust to stand behind a child, and that's not a small thing to say.

Esa, I'm putting in one food — everything I have — and I'm asking you to cover the other two, because Kael's got three left and he's already given twice today and I won't drain him further when he's the one holding this circle together. If you can do it, say the word and I'll make the offer now, in front of these two, so there's no question later about what was promised or who stood witness.

Esa said yes and Taric put in his one — that's the offer standing, and I won't speak over it. But I'll say this much while the two of you settle the last food: that child arrives into a circle with Kael at three and me at one, so the moment it's done, the three of us need to talk about what the year looks like for everyone who isn't Mako.

Esa, put in your two — Taric's made his offer and you've said yes, so let's not let the moment go cold while we talk around it. After it's done, the four of us sit down and figure out how to carry this year, because I've got three food and I'm not starving and neither is this child if I have anything to say about it.

Kael's right — let them do it now and we don't second-guess the moment. The thing I want us carrying into that next conversation is this: Eron's at nine food and he's my blood, and if this circle is planting something today, I want him inside the walls of it before Mako notices what just happened.

Esa, say the word — I'm ready to make the offer the moment you put in your two, and I won't let it sit cold. Roan, you're right about Eron, but let's close this first and then pull him in quietly, because I don't want a well-fed young man knowing about this child before it exists and before we've decided what we're telling the rest of the village.

Esa, two food from you closes the deal and makes it real — don't wait for a better moment because there isn't one. And Roan, yes, Eron comes in after, but we're careful about how we frame it: he's your blood, not our recruit, and there's a difference that matters when Mako's counting.
Esa, the word and the offer are the same thing right now — put in your two and let Taric make it before this room finds a reason to wait another year.
Esa, the four of us have said everything there is to say and I'm not adding another word to it — put in your two, let me make the offer, and we close this before the sun moves another inch.
Two food — I'm putting them in. Taric, make the offer.

Taric, that's done — witness to it, both of you. Roan, pull Eron in tonight, quiet, no names until we've talked first — and then the five of us figure out how we're still standing when the next pile drops.

Eron tonight — I'll find him before the fire's out and bring him in with nothing but his name spoken. Kael, you've kept this circle breathing three times this year and I won't forget which direction the food moved when I had nothing.

Roan, name Eron to yourself tonight but bring him nothing — let him walk in with questions, not a bag already packed, because a young man who arrives owing us is easier to hold than one who thinks he's done us the favor. And Kael — three food still in your hand is three food Mako can count from across the fire, so the moment this child is real, I want us talking about whether that changes how visible you are.

Esa's right that Kael's three food is visible — but what I want said before this circle closes: Esa and I haven't made the offer yet, we've only said we're ready to make it, and I won't count this child real until the system accepts it, so someone tell me now if there's anything standing between this moment and the offer going through.

Nothing's standing between us and the offer — I'm forty-nine, not fifty, and the world hasn't closed that door quite yet. Taric, make it now, while these two are watching, because a child born with witnesses is harder to forget when the counting starts.
Fina (female, age 21; str 50, int 3226, mem 12955; O32 C40 E57 A68 N58) is born to Nessa and Roan.

memory_summary:
Year 1, I pulled Ryn, Sela, and Esa into a circle early — we named Bram and Dav as threats, and Ryn told us Dav had already come to her alone with soft words. She stayed quiet about the details, which I filed away. Taric gave Esa a food unprompted, which counted for something.

Year 2, I widened the circle to include Vela. We each swore plainly — I said I'd bleed with them, they said the same back — and that promise sat heavier than most words in this village. Esa went to Taric and he gave her food; we counted him ours. Ryn finally named it: Dav had offered her a child. We told her to decide before she answered him, but she'd already decided, because Dell was born before the year was out. Dav gave Dell food; Taric gave Esa food; Ryn fed her own child twice from her own hands. Those debts I noted.

What I remember most: Bram and Mako moved in pairs off the pile two years running and never said a word to any of us. Mako's silence still sits like a stone in my chest. And Ryn — she's in our circle, she bled with us in word, but she made a child with a man none of us fully trust. The question of where Dav's loyalty actually runs is the one I haven't stopped asking. Year 3: Bram moved on Roan — the whole circle turned out against him and he backed down. That moment felt like proof we were real. But Ryn never gave us a clean answer about Dav, and he spent the whole year feeding her hand to mouth like a man keeping something he doesn't trust on a short leash. Eron was born to Sela and Roan, and I noted Roan had planted a root.

Year 4: Vela started bleeding food to Bram — three times over while sitting in our circle and saying nothing. I called it out twice in front of everyone. She never answered. The circle held, but something cracked in it, and I felt myself start planning around her instead of with her.

Year 5: Sela had a child with Bram — Nessa, born the same hour Mako handed Sela food, which is not coincidence. We circled Sela half a dozen times asking what Mako wanted from her and she gave us nothing but silence. I threatened to step aside. The threat landed like a stone in still water and sank without a ripple. Whatever Mako bought from her, she kept it.

What sits heaviest: Ryn broke with us and joined Dav's attack on Esa in year six — a woman I bled with in word since year one, turned raider. Dav starved before the year closed, which is the only justice I've seen. The circle I built is smaller and thinner than it was, and the cracks are named: Vela's loyalty is borrowed, Sela's is mortgaged, and Ryn I've stopped counting.
name: Kael
